title: P01 recurrent depth (Geiping et al. 2025): prelude + two shared core blocks applied r~U{1,2,3} times in training with prelude re-injection, r=3 (8 logical blocks) at sampling, on the 129-claude Lean incumbent (3,349,504 params)
description: P01 (idea ID P01, Geiping et al. 2025 recurrent depth): the six untied Peri-LN blocks become one prelude block, a two-block shared core applied r times with a Linear(2D,D) adapter on [state; prelude output] before each pass (init: their average), and one coda block; in training and RL fine-tune r is drawn uniformly from {1,2,3} per step (mean logical depth 6, same average FLOPs/step rate as the incumbent), while sampling and val (model.training False) always run r=3, i.e. 8 logical blocks. Unlike the six discarded fixed-depth loops (014, 028, 089, 105, 106, 125-fable), the model is trained to be a depth-robust refinement operator and gets two extra logical blocks of depth at sampling for free in pretraining wall-clock, which should help the >=7-line dev-transfer proofs that pretraining never saw.
hypothesis: Randomised recurrence trains the shared core as an iterative refinement of the proof state conditioned on the re-injected prelude output (Geiping et al. 2025 show loss keeps improving with more recurrences up to and slightly past the training mean). Expert iteration then samples with 8 logical blocks instead of 6 while pretraining paid for 6 on average, so longer proofs (>=7 lines, ~2x the pretraining chain length) get more sequential computation per token exactly where the metric is measured. Half the unique parameters (3.35M vs 4.8M) was nearly free in 125-fable (-14, noise-level), so capacity loss should be small. Failure modes: (a) depth-4 steps (r=1, a third of training) waste pretraining and the val loss at r=3 ends above the incumbent's ~0.080, giving a weaker RL start; (b) the core does not extrapolate/benefit from r=3 because it was only seen in a third of steps, so sampling at 8 blocks equals sampling at 6 while costing ~33% more sampling time; (c) the round-1 Lean parse-failure rate rises as in 125-fable (15% vs 13%) from the shared block.
expected_delta: -60 to +40 theorems at >=7 vs 646 (central guess -5); pretrain steps ~4100-4400 (same mean depth), final val loss at r=3 0.080-0.092; total secs 1800-2200 (sampling with 8 blocks ~33% slower per token)

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with recurrent-depth forward
arch.pos: hybrid: ALiBi slopes 1/4..1/256 on 4 heads, NoPE (slope 0) on 4 heads, no RoPE (unchanged from 115-fable)
arch.norm: Peri-LN layernorm (pre-LN plus LayerNorm on both branch outputs), unchanged
arch.change: vs 129-claude: 6 untied blocks -> [prelude, core_a, core_b, core_a, core_b, core_a, core_b, coda] with 4 unique blocks; adapter Linear(512,256,bias=False) init 0.5*[I I] applied to cat(state, prelude_out) before every core pass; r random in training (torch.randint on the global CPU RNG), R_MAX=3 at sampling/val
arch.n_params_detail: 4 PeriLN blocks x 790,784 = 3,163,136 + emb 27,392 + head 27,392 + ln_f 512 + adapter 131,072 = 3,349,504 (vocab 107); slopes buffer is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py, then blocks = ModuleList([prelude] + [core_a, core_b]*3 + [coda]) of PeriLNBlock with the same object aliases before load_state_dict (state_dict repeats the shared blocks under blocks.1/3/5 and blocks.2/4/6 keys)
arch.kv_cache: 8 caches, one per logical application (sample.generate builds one per model.blocks entry); caches[0] also holds key positions for the ALiBi bias as in 115-fable; CPU check: cached vs full forward max abs diff 8e-7
arch.n_layers_detail: 8 logical applications at sampling/val (1 prelude + 2x3 core + 1 coda); 4/6/8 logical in training (r~U{1,2,3}); 4 unique PeriLN blocks

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on the 4 unique blocks' matrices, head.weight and the new adapter.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorm params (unchanged from 129-claude except the adapter joins Muon)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock with floor 0.3 (unchanged from 129-claude): after 200 warmup steps lr = 1e-3*(0.3 + 0.35*(1+cos(pi*frac)))

data.augmentation: random ref shift (lean_seq names n1.. share one start offset per row)

config.init: fork default (normal 0.02, zero biases) then orthogonal_(gain=0.02*sqrt(max(shape))) on the 4 unique blocks' matrices; adapter 0.5*[I I]; emb/head normal 0.02

recurrence.train_r: uniform {1,2,3} per forward in training mode (pretrain and RL fine-tune)
